title: Sweep schedule + spot notes (personal runbook)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal sheet to schedule and record spot checks for a small hyperparameter sweep focused on batching and quantization interactions. Not intended as canonical experiment log — this is a fast scratchpad for runs I kick off and want to glance at during pairing or in Slack.

Experiment context:
- Product area: hosted-inference throughput improvements for chat endpoints.
- Goal: find batch + quant combo that reduces p95 latency < 120ms for seq<=512 while improving tokens/sec and lowering token cost ~10%.
- Constraints: use f32 baseline and 8-bit quant variants that are currently in the model catalog. Keep sequence length distribution real (20/60/20 split small/med/long).

Schedule (week of 2026-02-22):
- Mon: quick smoke, baseline f32 batches [1,2,4,8] on g4dn-ish instance.
- Tue: run 8-bit quant variants same batches.
- Wed: mixed-batch trials (batcher warmup + dynamic batching enabled).
- Thu: prefix/KV cache on/off compare for common prefixes.
- Fri: summarize, pick 2 promising configs for canary.

Compact run table (rows are my quick paste-in from the runner output):
run_id,model,quant,batch,seq,avg_lat_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1k_tok,notes
R001,gpt-small,f32,1,64,55,88,180,0.018,baseline single request
R002,gpt-small,f32,4,64,60,120,640,0.024,batching increases p95 due to head-of-line
R003,gpt-small,8bit,4,64,48,95,820,0.015,quant improves throughput but p95 noisy
R004,gpt-small,8bit,8,64,62,140,1500,0.012,p95 jumps at high batch (queueing)
R005,gpt-med,8bit,2,256,110,170,430,0.034,seq=256 close to target but cost up
R006,gpt-small,8bit,4,512,210,320,300,0.045,long seq, misses latency SLO
R007,gpt-small,f32,2,64,52,90,360,0.02,kicker: enabling continuous-batching reduced avg by ~6ms
R008,gpt-small,8bit,4,64,50,98,800,0.014,repeat of R003 with cache warming

Quick observations:
- 8-bit quant consistently improves tokens/sec and reduces cost-per-1k, but p95 variance increases in some high-batch/high-concurrency scenarios.
- Best trade-off in these small runs: 8bit + batch=4 with dynamic batcher and prefix cache warmed (see R003/R008).
- For seq<=512, avoid batch=8 unless we can guarantee concurrency isolation or use reserved pool.

Spot commands & notes (copy-paste friendly):
- run locally: ./run_sweep.sh --model gpt-small --quant 8bit --batches 1,2,4,8 --seqs 64,256
- profiler: REDWOOD_PROF=1 go run ./cmd/infer --profile-output=~/tmp/profile.json
- quick cost calc (rough): cost_per_1k = (gpu_min_cost_per_hour / (tokens_per_sec*3600)) * 1000

Hypotheses to test next:
- H1: Enabling kv-prefix caching (sticky for repeated users) will drop p95 by 10-20% for seq<=128 without lowering throughput.
- H2: Quantization-induced jitter is dominated by kernel selection path; pinning a stable kernel set will reduce p95 variance.

Immediate next steps (short checklist):
- [ ] Re-run R003 with concurrency=1/4 to see if p95 tail is concurrency-related (assigned to self).
- [ ] Add p50/p90/p99 columns in the runner summary (ticket INF-679).
- [ ] Schedule 30-min pairing with Maya to test reserved pool behavior for batch=8.

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- Are we measuring p95 from single replica or end-to-end (incl. routing/queueing)? Need to align with SRE metrics.
- Is the cost estimate using pre-emptible pricing? Use consistent pricing model when comparing.
- How do inference kernel fallbacks show up in traces? Add trace id to the runner logs.

Versioning & anchors:
- quick snapshot saved to /tmp/sweep-R003-R008-2026-02-23.log (local).
- canonical infra ticket: JIRA-INF-672 (linked above).

Casual notes (brain dump, keep below):
- If R003 repeats under 5 trials w/ similar p95, propose canary config for hosted with 10% traffic.
- Remember to capture a small sample of outputs for quality checks (prompt set: onboarding-welcome, help-article-summary).

End of sheet — this is a live scratchpad. Delete or convert to formal runlog when polished.
